questions.stem: With reference to the Governor's power to sanction prosecution of a Minister or former Minister under the Prevention of Corruption Act, consider the following two statements:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually accurate: courts have held (e.g., Mansukhlal Vithaldas Chauhan v. State of Gujarat and the later Jayalalithaa sanction litigation) that a Governor may act in personal discretion under Article 163 while deciding on sanction to prosecute a Minister, precisely because the Council of Ministers cannot be an impartial judge of its own colleague's conduct — this is why Statement-I's requirement of the Governor's own approval (rather than Cabinet advice) was the correct route. Statement-II directly supplies that reasoning, so it explains Statement-I. The Kerala case, where the Governor acted on the Chief Minister's request independent of routine Cabinet advice, fits this established constitutional position.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Messi visit case: Keralam Governor gives approval to prosecute former Sports Minister Abdurahiman over alleged irregularities
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 163 gubernatorial discretion and Section 17A/19 PC Act sanction requirement; similar to UPSC 2023 Statement-I/II items on constitutional functionaries' discretionary powers

questions.stem: With reference to India's Flexible Inflation Targeting framework, which came into focus after retail inflation breached the RBI's upper tolerance limit, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under the amended RBI Act, 1934, the inflation target is fixed by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI once every five years, and is currently 4% with a tolerance band of +/-2%.
The Monetary Policy Committee is chaired by the Union Finance Secretary and comprises three officials of the Finance Ministry and three external members appointed by the RBI.

If average inflation remains outside the tolerance band for three consecutive quarters, the RBI is deemed to have failed to meet the target and must send a report to the Central Government explaining the reasons and proposed remedial action.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 and 3 are correct: the inflation target (4% +/-2%) is notified by the Government in consultation with the RBI for five-year blocks, and three-consecutive-quarter failure triggers a mandatory report to the Central Government under Section 45ZN of the RBI Act. Statement 2 is wrong — the Monetary Policy Committee is chaired by the RBI Governor, with three RBI officials and three members appointed by the Central Government, not the Finance Secretary or Finance Ministry officials.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Retail inflation hits 6.09% in October, crosses RBI's upper tolerance limit
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Flexible Inflation Targeting framework and MPC composition, a recurring theme since UPSC 2022's monetary policy questions

questions.stem: India has been projected as the only major emitter whose carbon emissions will rise in 2026 even as global emissions fall. In this context, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Global Carbon Budget report, which tracks such emission trends, is published annually by the Global Carbon Project, an international research collaboration, and not by the UNFCCC Secretariat.
India has formally committed, as part of its Nationally Determined Contributions, to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.
India's updated Nationally Determined Contributions include a target of reducing the emissions intensity of its GDP by 45% by 2030 compared to 2005 levels.
India's current per capita carbon dioxide emissions are higher than the global average per capita emissions.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Global Carbon Project (not the UNFCCC Secretariat) publishes the annual Global Carbon Budget, and India's updated NDC targets a 45% cut in emissions intensity of GDP by 2030 over 2005 levels. Statement 2 is wrong because India's net-zero pledge, announced at COP26, is for 2070, not 2050. Statement 4 is wrong because India's per capita emissions remain well below the global average, despite its large absolute and rising emissions.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Global carbon emissions are set to fall. Why are India’s emissions projected to rise?
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's climate commitments (NDC, net-zero target) and the Global Carbon Project as publishing body, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on COP outcomes and emission reports

questions.stem: A new wearable device claims to track cerebral blood flow using a sensing technology called Photoplethysmography (PPG), the same core technology found in smartwatches. Which one of the following best describes PPG?
options: An electrical sensing technique that records the heart's rhythm by measuring the difference in electrical potential between electrodes placed on the skin over the chest
An imaging technique that uses magnetic fields and radio waves to generate detailed cross-sectional images of soft tissue, including blood vessels in the brain
An optical sensing technique that detects changes in blood volume in tissue by measuring variations in the amount of light absorbed or reflected as blood pulses with each heartbeat
An ultrasound-based technique that measures the velocity of blood flow in arteries by analysing the Doppler shift of reflected sound waves
questions.explanation: PPG is correctly described by option 3 — it shines light into the skin and analyses the reflected/absorbed signal to infer blood-volume changes with each heartbeat, as the article explains. Option 1 describes electrocardiography (ECG), option 2 describes MRI, and option 4 describes Doppler ultrasound — all are genuine but distinct medical sensing technologies, not PPG.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Deepinder Goyal's Temple: Can a wearable really measure blood flow inside your brain?
questions.pyqLink: Tests distinguishing common biomedical sensing technologies, similar in spirit to UPSC 2019's 'best describes the term' format applied to technical jargon

questions.stem: A recent Supreme Court verdict on inheritance of ancestral property revisited core concepts of Hindu personal law. Consider the following pairs:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Mitakshara school
Historically prevalent in most parts of India (except Bengal and Assam); recognised a right by birth for a son in coparcenary property
Dayabhaga school
Historically prevalent in Bengal and Assam; a son acquired no right in ancestral property by birth, title accruing only on the father's death
Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005
Conferred upon a daughter the same coparcenary rights by birth in ancestral property as a son
Coparcenary
A legal institution under Hindu law comprising persons who acquire an interest in joint family property by birth, membership of which now extends to daughters as well
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Mitakshara and Dayabhaga schools differ precisely on whether a son's right in ancestral property arises by birth or only on the father's death; the 2005 Amendment extended coparcenary birthright to daughters; and coparcenary, as a birth-based interest in joint family property, now includes daughters as members. The recent Supreme Court ruling (that a grandson cannot claim a share if the father, himself an heir, received the property via partition/compromise deed) rests on exactly this distinction between ancestral and self-acquired property.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Can a Hindu man automatically claim share in his grandfather’s property? What SC held
questions.pyqLink: Tests schools of Hindu law and the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005 — a recurring Indian Society/personal law theme in Prelims

questions.stem: Kolhapur district in Maharashtra, home to the Gokul dairy cooperative at the centre of a recent election controversy, is a well-known geographical and economic region of the state. Consider the following statements about it:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Kolhapur district is located in the southern part of Maharashtra, within the Desh (upland plateau) region of the Deccan Plateau.
Kolhapur city is situated on the bank of the Godavari river.
Kolhapur district shares an international border with Goa.
Kolhapur is primarily known for cotton textile production and has no notable dairy or sugarcane economy.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct — Kolhapur lies in the southern Desh plateau region of Maharashtra. Statement 2 is wrong: Kolhapur city stands on the Panchganga river, a tributary of the Krishna, not the Godavari. Statement 3 is wrong: Goa is an Indian state, so the Kolhapur-Goa boundary is an inter-state, not an international, border. Statement 4 is wrong: Kolhapur is in fact a major sugarcane-growing and dairy-producing (Gokul) region, not primarily a cotton textile centre.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Gokul dairy: The controversy over elections to Maharashtra’s largest milk cooperative
questions.pyqLink: Tests physical/economic geography of a Deccan Plateau district and river-tributary relationships, a recurring Mapping/Physical Geography theme

questions.stem: Andhra Pradesh's move to enact India's first state law to protect investors has drawn attention to the broader framework of investor protection in India. In this context, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under India's Model Bilateral Investment Treaty, 2016, a foreign investor can directly approach international arbitration as soon as a dispute arises, without first exhausting domestic remedies.

India's Model Bilateral Investment Treaty, 2016 excludes taxation measures and certain general public policy matters, such as compulsory licensing, from the scope of protected 'investment' available to foreign investors.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: India's Model BIT, 2016 narrowed the definition of 'investment' and carved out taxation measures and several sovereign/public-policy matters, including compulsory licensing, from investor-protection coverage. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Model BIT actually requires a foreign investor to first exhaust domestic judicial or administrative remedies, typically for five years, before invoking international arbitration — a deliberate departure from older BITs that allowed near-immediate recourse to Investor-State Dispute Settlement.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: 'New state law to shield investors in Andhra Pradesh'
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's Model Bilateral Investment Treaty, 2016 and ISDS safeguards, linked to UPSC's past questions on international economic agreements and investment law

questions.stem: With reference to the arrest of an Indian Air Force officer for allegedly sharing classified war-plan documents with a suspected Pakistani intelligence operative, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Official Secrets Act, 1923 can be invoked against the disclosure of information prejudicial to the safety or interests of the State, even if that information was not formally classified as 'secret'.
Statement-II: The Right to Information Act, 2005 explicitly repealed the espionage-related provisions of the Official Secrets Act, 1923.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: Section 3 of the OSA, 1923 covers espionage-type disclosures of information useful to an enemy or prejudicial to State safety, regardless of formal classification — exactly the provision invoked against the Wing Commander for sharing war plans and deployment details. Statement-II is incorrect: the RTI Act, 2005 (Section 22) merely gives RTI an overriding effect over other laws for disclosure purposes; it did not repeal the OSA, 1923, which remains the operative law in this case.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: IAF officer shared war plans, deployment details with Pak operative: Police to court
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Official Secrets Act, 1923 and its relationship with the RTI Act, 2005 — similar to UPSC's recurring questions on overriding clauses between statutes.

questions.stem: With reference to India's flexible inflation-targeting framework, following October's retail inflation print above the Reserve Bank of India's tolerance limit, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The RBI's inflation target under the framework is 4% Consumer Price Index inflation, with a tolerance band of plus/minus 2 percentage points.
The RBI is statutorily deemed to have failed its mandate if average inflation remains outside the tolerance band for three consecutive quarters.
The Monetary Policy Committee consists of four officials from the RBI and three members nominated by the Central Government.
If the inflation target is missed, the Central Government is empowered to directly revise the policy repo rate in place of the Monetary Policy Committee.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct and match the RBI Act provisions reflected in the article (target of 4% with a 2-6% tolerance band; 'failure' triggers after three consecutive quarters outside this band). Statement 3 is wrong: the MPC has six members — the Governor, one Deputy Governor and one RBI-nominated official (three from the RBI) plus three external members nominated by the Government, not four and three. Statement 4 is wrong: even after a target failure, the repo rate is set only by MPC vote; the Government's role is limited to receiving an explanatory report, not setting the rate itself.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Flight tickets, food and more: 5 charts that explain what’s driving inflation higher, wider
questions.pyqLink: Tests the RBI's flexible inflation-targeting framework and MPC composition — a recurring Economy PYQ theme (e.g., UPSC 2022 on MPC/monetary policy).

questions.stem: The Assam government's admission that forest land was diverted for police commando camps in 'gross violation' of forest laws draws attention to India's forest-clearance architecture. Consider the following pairs:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
Requires prior approval of the Central Government before forest land is diverted to non-forest use
Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAMPA)
Funded mainly through Net Present Value and compensatory afforestation payments collected from entities diverting forest land
Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 2023
Renamed and amended version of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
Regional Office, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Functions as the Ministry's field-level monitoring arm, overseeing compliance with forest clearance conditions
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correctly matched. The 1980 Act (renamed the Van Adhiniyam in 2023) mandates Central approval for forest diversion; CAMPA funds come from NPV/compensatory-afforestation levies on project proponents, not general budgetary grants; and the Ministry's regional office acts exactly as the article shows — it directed the Assam forest department to take legal action against the officer for authorising commando camps on forest land without such approval.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Assam: Retired forest officer on repeated extensions to be put in mines department now
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional architecture of the Forest (Conservation) Act/Van Adhiniyam and CAMPA — static-current fusion in the mould of UPSC's pairs-matched format on environmental legislation.

questions.stem: With reference to trapped-ion quantum computing, a field recognised in this year's Infosys Prize for work on building programmable quantum systems using trapped ions, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Trapped-ion qubits are typically cooled to operating temperature using liquid-helium dilution refrigerators, the same technique used for superconducting qubits.
Quantum superposition allows a qubit to represent the states 0 and 1 simultaneously, unlike a classical bit which can only be in one state at a time.
Quantum entanglement produces correlations between qubits such that the measured state of one qubit is linked to the measured state of another entangled qubit, even when physically separated.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect: trapped-ion qubits are confined by electromagnetic (Paul/RF) traps in ultra-high vacuum and cooled mainly through laser cooling, not through liquid-helium dilution refrigerators — that cryogenic method is characteristic of superconducting-circuit qubits, a competing quantum-computing architecture. Statements 2 and 3 correctly describe superposition and entanglement, the two defining quantum-mechanical properties exploited by qubits of any physical implementation.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Six, including quantum and climate change researchers, win Infosys Prize
questions.pyqLink: Tests basic quantum-computing concepts (qubit, superposition, entanglement, trapped-ion vs superconducting platforms) now entering the UPSC S&T syllabus as emerging technology.

questions.stem: Kashmiri Wazas (traditional chefs) have recently decided to stop serving wedding feasts after 10 pm. With reference to Jammu & Kashmir's cultural heritage, which one of the following best describes 'Wazwan'?
options: A Geographical Indication-tagged variety of saffron cultivated in the Karewa uplands of the Kashmir valley
A folk dance performance traditionally staged during Kashmiri marriage ceremonies by professional performers called Wazas
A traditional multi-course non-vegetarian feast served at Kashmiri weddings, prepared by hereditary chefs known as Wazas, comprising dishes such as Rista, Tabakhmaaz and Goshtaba
A ceremonial handicraft textile presented to the bride's family as part of Kashmiri wedding rituals
questions.explanation: Wazwan is the elaborate multi-course non-vegetarian feast central to Kashmiri weddings, traditionally prepared and served by hereditary chefs called Wazas, with signature dishes like Rista, Tabakhmaaz, Roganjosh and Goshtaba, as described in the article. The other options misattribute the term to Kashmiri saffron (a separate GI product), a dance form, or a textile craft — none of which the Wazas are associated with.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: No meal after 10 pm: Kashmiri wedding chefs have had enough of late-night feasts
questions.pyqLink: Tests identification of a regional cultural/culinary tradition — in the style of UPSC's recurring questions on GI tags, festivals and traditional practices of Indian states.

questions.stem: With reference to the Siang river and the protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Yarlung Tsangpo river of Tibet becomes known as the Siang upon entering India through Arunachal Pradesh.
The Siang drains into the Bay of Bengal independently of the Brahmaputra, through a separate delta system in Assam.
The proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is located in the Dibang Valley district of Arunachal Pradesh.
The Siang river system is classified as part of the Ganga river basin under India's river basin classification.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct: the Yarlung Tsangpo is renamed the Siang on entering Arunachal Pradesh. Statement 2 is wrong — the Siang joins the Dibang and Lohit rivers in Assam to form the Brahmaputra; it does not drain independently. Statement 3 is wrong — SUMP is proposed in the Siang Valley districts (e.g., Upper/East Siang), not Dibang Valley district. Statement 4 is wrong — the Siang belongs to the Brahmaputra basin, a basin distinct from the Ganga basin in India's river classification.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Out after month in detention, Siang activist Adum Tayong says stir will continue
questions.pyqLink: Tests river-system geography (Yarlung Tsangpo-Siang-Brahmaputra continuum and basin classification) — a frequent UPSC Geography theme on transboundary rivers.

questions.stem: With reference to PM Modi's upcoming visit to Manila for the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The ASEAN-India Summit is held annually, bringing together India and the ten member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
The East Asia Summit comprises the ten ASEAN member states along with India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and the European Union, but excludes the United States and Russia.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the ASEAN-India Summit, now in its 23rd edition, is an annual mechanism between India and all ten ASEAN members. Statement 2 is incorrect: the East Asia Summit's eight non-ASEAN members are India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, the United States and Russia; the European Union is not a member, while the US and Russia — which the statement wrongly excludes — are founding participants.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India news Live Updates, 13 November 2026: Severe air quality grips Delhi as AIIMS AQI hits 418
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional composition of ASEAN-led forums (ASEAN-India Summit vs East Asia Summit) — a recurring IR theme on regional groupings' membership.

questions.stem: Gold prices are tracked daily across Indian cities in terms of 24, 22 and 18 carat variants. With reference to gold purity and the hallmarking of gold jewellery in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Hallmarking of gold jewellery and artefacts is mandated under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Act, 2016.
The Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number assigned to hallmarked gold jewellery is a six-digit alphanumeric code.
24 carat gold, being the purest form, is commonly used for making jewellery because of its hardness and durability.
Hallmarking of gold jewellery is mandatory across all districts of India with no exemptions whatsoever.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: hallmarking operates under the BIS Act, 2016, and the HUID is indeed a six-digit alphanumeric code. Statement 3 is wrong because 24 carat (999 purity) gold is soft and malleable, so 22 carat (916) gold, alloyed for strength, is preferred for jewellery. Statement 4 is wrong because exemptions exist, such as for jewellery below 2 grams, exports, and certain categories like watches and fountain pens.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Gold Rate Today, November 13: Check 18, 22 and 24 carat gold prices in Chennai, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and other cities
questions.pyqLink: Tests BIS hallmarking framework and carat purity, similar in spirit to UPSC's recurring questions on BIS standards and consumer protection mechanisms.

questions.stem: With reference to India's tuberculosis (TB) elimination efforts in the context of the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Global Tuberculosis Report is published annually by the World Health Organization to track the global TB burden.
India's National Strategic Plan sets a target to eliminate tuberculosis by 2025, five years ahead of the global Sustainable Development Goal target of 2030.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The WHO brings out the Global Tuberculosis Report every year, and the article itself references the 'Global Tuberculosis Report 2026,' confirming its annual nature. India has set an accelerated national target of eliminating TB by 2025, ahead of the global SDG target of 2030, as part of its National TB Elimination Programme.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's TB elimination targets versus global SDG targets, a recurring health-governance theme in UPSC Prelims (e.g., 2020 questions on TB treatment trends).

questions.stem: The Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) has awarded a contract for a Transit-Oriented Development project at Thirumangalam. With reference to the institutional and policy framework of urban metro rail in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Metro rail corporations in India, such as Chennai Metro Rail Limited, are typically incorporated as companies under the Companies Act, with equity shared between the Union and State Governments.
The Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) policy is administered exclusively by the Ministry of Railways to promote commercial development only around railway stations.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: metro corporations like CMRL are joint-venture companies of the Union and State Governments, registered under the Companies Act. Statement 2 is incorrect because the TOD policy referenced in the article is administered by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), not the Ministry of Railways, and it applies broadly to transit stations including metro systems, not exclusively to railway stations.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Chennai Metro's Thirumangalam project to feature train running through the building
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory/company status of urban transit bodies and ministry jurisdiction, akin to past questions distinguishing statutory, constitutional and executive bodies.

questions.stem: The report on Tarluvada village notes that much of the land given to landless Dalit families was 'D-patta' (assigned land) granted during Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's time. With reference to land reform measures in post-independence India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: D-patta refers to land assigned by the government to landless persons, including Dalits, under land distribution programmes.
Zamindari Abolition Acts passed by various states after independence sought to abolish intermediary tenures and establish a direct relationship between the state and cultivators.
The Bhoodan movement initiated by Vinoba Bhave involved the government compulsorily acquiring surplus land from zamindars for redistribution to the landless.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct descriptions of assigned land schemes and the Zamindari Abolition Acts. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Bhoodan movement relied on voluntary donation of land by landowners persuaded by Vinoba Bhave, not compulsory government acquisition — compulsory acquisition of surplus land was instead the mechanism under land ceiling legislation.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada's blue wall in Visakhapatnam
questions.pyqLink: Tests post-independence land reform measures (Zamindari abolition, Bhoodan, land ceiling) — a recurring Modern India theme distinguishing voluntary versus statutory land redistribution.

questions.stem: The hill called Chukka Konda near Visakhapatnam has been stripped and terraced for construction of a hyperscale data centre. With reference to Indian environmental regulation of such large infrastructure and land-use change, consider the following pairs:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
Regulates diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes, requiring prior Central Government approval
Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006
Mandates prior environmental clearance for specified categories of developmental projects
Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016
Provides for funds collected to compensate for forest land diverted to non-forest use
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) Notification
Regulates industrial and infrastructure activities within 10 km of every state's political boundary
questions.explanation: The first three pairs are correctly matched: the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 governs forest land diversion, the EIA Notification, 2006 mandates environmental clearance for listed project categories, and the CAF Act, 2016 funds compensatory afforestation. The fourth pair is incorrect because the CRZ Notification regulates activities in coastal zones near the sea, tidal water bodies and backwaters — not within 10 km of state political boundaries.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada's blue wall in Visakhapatnam
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory instruments governing land diversion and environmental clearance for large infrastructure, a frequent pairs-matching theme since 2022-23.

questions.stem: Visakhapatnam, where land has been cleared for a hyperscale data centre, lies amid the Eastern Ghats. With reference to the physiography of India, which one of the following best describes the Eastern Ghats?
options: A continuous, unbroken range of fold mountains running parallel to the east coast, higher in elevation than the Western Ghats
A discontinuous and comparatively low series of hill ranges running along India's eastern coast, dissected by major east-flowing rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi
A range of relict mountains formed primarily of volcanic basalt, similar in geological origin to the Deccan Trap
A range of young fold mountains formed due to the collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates
questions.explanation: The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous, eroded and comparatively low range, broken into segments by major east-flowing rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi, unlike the continuous and higher Western Ghats. Option C wrongly attributes a Deccan Trap-like volcanic basalt origin, and option D describes the Himalayas, not the Eastern Ghats.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada's blue wall in Visakhapatnam
questions.pyqLink: Tests the physiographic distinction between the Eastern and Western Ghats, a standard Indian physical geography theme recurring in UPSC Prelims.
